title: Home
text:
Welcome to my portfolio for MUSA 5080: Public Policy Analytics at the University of Pennsylvania.
This site documents my work in the Master of Urban Spatial Analytics program — weekly notes, course assignments, and a final project applying data analysis to urban policy questions.







I’m a MUSA (Master’s of Urban Spatial Analytics) student at the University of Pennsylvania. My background is in urban planning and design.




Spatial analysis, GIS, data visualisation, urban design, quantitative methods.
Tools: QGIS; R; Python; Adobe Suite; Google Earth Engine; Stata






Weekly Notes — what I’m learning each week
Assignments — analyses completed for the course
About — more background and how to reach me






Email: chlauryn@upenn.edu
GitHub: @chlauryn

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Three places a file can live:

My computer - where I edit
GitHub.com - where it’s stored
My live site - what the world sees

Types of files and folders:

For me - index.qmd, about.qmd, weekly_notes.qmd, assignments.qmd
For the machine - quarto.yml (settings for whole website), _freeze (for quarto memory, after it gets rendered), .Rproj (for RStudio), .gitignore (for github), Renviron (for R, to keep secrets), docs/ (The Internet)

The loop: Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Reflection

I have done spatial analysis in R before but only in RScript (and then manually exported into InDesign) without using github. I am excited about using Quarto to create a more seamless transition into Github.com and other digital media.
One thing I’m nervous about: Saving all the files in the right place!

title: Week 1: Getting Set Up
text:
Today’s workflow


Copy github template from lecturer
Template button → clone
Name github folder. Public
On personal github, click Code → open with github desktop → clone onto LOCAL computer
On file explorer, open Rproj folder → open on RStudio
Make changes on like /qmd or /yml files. Then save as you go
When you are all done, click Render, then it will save to LOCAL website.
Then go to Github desktop → commit changes → Push button
Then if you make the website page, it should show there
Github → settings → pages → website link should be there
TO CREATE WEBSITE: deploy from a branch → main branch → /docs (which is a folder of html files that make a website) → save
